reading.body:
DartPoints Columbus publishes 2.5 MW of IT capacity, representing the only megawatt figure disclosed by any data center operator in Indiana, though this reflects a data gap rather than market dominance.

The facility sits in Columbus, Indiana at a regional operator focused on Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets outside major metros. DartPoints operates 11 facilities across 10 states following its April 2025 acquisition by NOVA Infrastructure, which committed more than 250 million dollars in combined growth capital alongside real estate acquisition in three states. The operator emphasizes AI-ready, high-density infrastructure, though the Columbus location's specifications beyond IT capacity remain unpublished.

2.5 MW translates to roughly 63 racks at 40 kW per rack, a density appropriate for AI training workloads, or roughly 250 racks at 10 kW per rack, typical for colocation. Without facility-level electrical specifications or cooling capacity data, the effective density and workload suitability cannot be assessed from published sources. No security certifications are listed, limiting inference about regulated or sensitive workload hosting.

The absence of published capacity figures from five other Indiana data centers means this site cannot rank regional infrastructure by actual supply. The data shows only that DartPoints Columbus chose to disclose, not what the state's total computing footprint comprises.
